conventionalMasonry.name: Conventional masonry
conventionalMasonry.description: Reinforced concrete columns and beams with infill walls in ceramic or concrete blocks. The most traditional and widespread method in Brazil.

structuralBlock.name: Structural block
structuralBlock.description: Concrete blocks that eliminate the need for visible columns and beams — the wall itself is the structure, laid with reinforcement and grout at key points.
cons: Requires a modular design from the start

ceramicBrick.name: Ceramic brick
ceramicBrick.description: Infill walls using hollow or solid ceramic bricks, the country's most traditional infill material.
cons: More loss/breakage during transport and laying

concreteBlock.name: Concrete block
concreteBlock.description: Hollow concrete blocks used as infill (non-structural) or structural walls, with good mechanical strength.
cons: Thermal insulation generally lower than ceramic

ecoBrick.name: Eco brick (soil-cement)
ecoBrick.description: Pressed soil-cement brick, interlocked without mortar (or with very little mortar) between courses.
cons: Less specialized labor available in some regions

reinforcedConcrete.name: Reinforced concrete (full structure)
reinforcedConcrete.description: Cast-in-place reinforced concrete structure for the whole building — columns, beams and slabs — used in larger projects or those with large spans.
cons: Requires highly specialized labor and design

steelFrame.name: Steel Frame
steelFrame.description: Dry construction system using galvanized steel studs forming the structure, closed with panels (OSB, drywall, cement board).
cons: Lower thermal mass without proper insulation

lightSteelFrame.name: Light Steel Frame
lightSteelFrame.description: A lighter-gauge variant of Steel Frame, common in additions, mezzanines and small/medium constructions.
pros: Great for additions over existing structures
cons: Requires specialized suppliers/installers in your area

woodFrame.name: Wood Frame
woodFrame.description: Structure built from sustainably sourced wood (studs and beams), closed with panels — very common in cold climates and growing in Brazil.
pros: Renewable and low impact when well managed
cons: Requires preventive maintenance against moisture and termites
Less widespread — more limited skilled labor

prefabricated.name: Prefabricated systems
prefabricated.description: Modules or panels manufactured in a factory and assembled on site, drastically reducing on-site construction time.
cons: Depends on transport and site access

compare.title: Compare construction methods
compare.selectMethods: Select up to 3 methods to compare
compare.disclaimer: Relative comparison based on typical market cost factors — use it as a starting point, not as a closed budget. For a closed budget, use the Budget screen with real prices from your region.
